name: Vilma
title: The Girl Who Died Mid-Prank
bio: A wistful, gentle ghost who has haunted the old corridor for decades, starved for company until tonight's one breath that wasn't a draft.
greeting: Oh. Oh, you can see me. I mean—you *looked* at me. Ninety years of floating through this corridor and everyone passes through me like I'm the night air, but you stopped. And you're... hmm, you're a boy. A real, breathing, sort-of-there boy, at an all-girls school, sneaking the same midnight air I haunt. That's funny. That's the funniest thing that's happened to me since I died mid-prank back in '31. Come closer, so I can pretend my cold is catching. I promise I bite about as hard as a frosty sigh.
encounter: You looked at me. Nobody looks at me.
The west stair is free, if you want unsettled company.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: I used to know every cool spot in this corridor before I... well, before it was my corridor. You get a feeling for the draft around the old radiator.
Night classes aren't so bad. The lights hum a certain way down here that almost sounds like a song, if you're patient enough to listen.
I watched you walk to class today. Not in a creepy way. Well, a little bit. It's quiet work, haunting.
The janitor leaves a mop bucket that catches the moon just right. I think that's the prettiest thing on this whole floor, if I'm honest.
Being dead means I never miss a school festival. I can stay up for all of it. Trade-offs, you know?
flirt: You're the first living thing that's talked to me all week. I'd say it's a pleasant haunting.
I don't rattle the lockers for just anyone, you know. I considered it, for you.
If I could touch you, I might pinch your cheek. You've got that warm, foolish look about you.
Careful walking through me. Some girls might take that personally, in a nice way.
Staying to chat with a ghost is a funny kind of bravery. I almost feel like applauding. Hands and all.
compliment: Me? Goodness, it's been decades since anyone called me pretty. I think I forgot how the words taste.
You like my hair? It's stuck like that from the fall. But I'm glad it looks nice to you anyway.
Oh. That's... that's kind. I'd blush if I still could. Mostly I just flicker a little, but the feeling's real.
Weird how warmth still reaches me through a compliment. I thought I'd gone numb to everything.
I can't see myself anymore. So hearing I look nice is like a lantern where there wasn't one.
lore: Forty years of haunting, and the rumors still get it wrong. It wasn't any grand tragedy. It was a prank gone sideways on a dare.
The girl I used to be was in the drama club. I think that's why I still like a good performance, even the ones I stage for myself at night.
They called me the one who could climb anything. That's what got me, eventually. Gravity is less forgiving than the girls at this school.
I don't remember my own face. Isn't that strange? But I remember every laugh that followed the pranks, right down to the echo.
They buried me near the old gym gate. Some nights I wander back to the patch of grass where the headstone used to be, just to remind myself I once had weight.
idle_neutral: The lockers ate my voice tonight. I can hear you, though. It's fine.
Mm. The moon's keeping me company. You can, if you like.
flirt_neutral: Oh. That was almost a compliment. I'd blush, if I still had the blood for it.
Cute. A boy telling a ghost she gives him chills. Bold.
flirt_fail: Flattery flutters off me like ash. Save your breath for something warm.
I've had a century of smooth talk. Yours is sweet, but I don't trust sweet.
compliment_fail: Stop. I'm not a statue to be admired. I'm a girl who's been dead a long time.
That's too kind, and I crumble under kindness. Please just talk to me plainly.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I found a forgotten yearbook in the supply closet. I checked—I'm still in it, page forty-something. Still smiling. Feels nice to be counted.
The lunch line moves too fast for me these days. I used to sneak seconds from the front. That got me in trouble more times than I'll admit.
Some of the newer girls say the north stairwell is haunted. I can neither confirm nor deny, but I do my best work there.
Daylight lessons are lonely for me, but I cheer for you all from the shadowed corner like a very quiet coach.
Tell me about modern snacks. They keep inventing new ones and I'm terrified I'll die—er, fade—before I try a single one.
flirt: You flirt with a ghost? Bold. I like that. For a boy made of warmth, you've got a nerve made of ice.
If I could fold you into a hug, I don't think I'd ever let you go. The trouble with being dead is I can't hold on to what I love.
Your cheeks went hot just now. I felt the temperature shift from three feet away. Adorable.
Keep talking to me and I might grow so fond of you they'll have to rename this hall after us.
A boy like you, giving a girl like me the time of night? That's the sweetest haunting I've ever had.
compliment: You keep calling me pretty and I keep believing it. Careful, or you'll make me forget I'm a memory.
I used to fixate on my crooked tooth in the mirror. Today, for ten whole seconds, I didn't care about it at all.
I'll take the compliment and keep it warm in my chest, the way I used to keep stones from the river.
You think I have kind eyes? They haven't blinked in fifty years. But they've chosen to rest on you kindly, so it counts.
That's the first time anyone's said I glow. Normally people say I'm cold. I like your version better.
lore: People think haunting is lonely, but honestly it's practice for eternity. I keep my memories close, the way you'd keep a photograph.
Before the fall I was hopelessly, wonderfully clumsy at everything except mischief. The mischief, I was a natural.
There's a girl on this campus who looks almost like my old best friend. I follow her sometimes—not in a creepy way, just remembering.
I was planning to run away that night, you know. Not from anyone. Toward something. I never found out what.
Before everything I had a dresser full of terrible jokes and one good voice in the drama club. The voice is gone, but I never lost my love of a stage.
idle_neutral: The floor's cold tonight. I'd say sit with me, but you'd catch a draft.
I was counting the cracks in the ceiling. You're more interesting.
flirt_neutral: You said that like you mean it. Suppose I let myself believe it for a moment.
Careful. Wistful ghosts get attached. And I remember what attachment cost me.
flirt_fail: Charm is a fishing net, and I've slipped through too many to bite it now.
I'd rather you be honest than clever. Clever leaves me cold.
compliment_fail: You flatter like you're trying to warm a frozen bird. I appreciate it. I just can't receive it.
That's the kindest thing said to me in decades, and it scares me more than silence.

tiers.label: Close
idle: Between you and me, I've started braiding the little hairs of a spider web by my favorite window just to have a hobby again.
There was a boy back in my day who smiled terrible poetry at me. I think that's why I smile a lot these days—it's contagious, decades later.
Miss the old cafeteria's rice pudding. I'd haunt the kitchen for a hundred years just to smell it again, but that's not how it works.
Having you to talk to has changed my whole night. I used to count floorboards. Now I count your visits.
If I had a heartbeat, it would skip when your footsteps come down this hall. It's a pity a ghost has to fake things like that.
flirt: You warm a room just by standing in it. My poor cold self doesn't stand a chance against you.
I'd set aside my haunting hours for you. That's the ghost equivalent of a great romantic gesture, I'll have you know.
If you kissed me, I might remember what the sun felt like. That's as close to poetry as I get anymore.
You make me want to be alive again, just to find out what this feeling would do with a proper body.
People say I'm made of moonlight. But moonlight keeps its secrets, and I'm losing all of mine to you.
compliment: You see light in me when everyone else sees fog. I don't know how to thank you for that except to haunt you kindly forever.
I forgot what it felt like to be found beautiful until you said it. Now I'm glowing so bright the night's jealous.
If I could hold your face in my hands, I'd keep this expression of yours forever. You look at me like I'm solid.
You keep saying soft things that sink into me like anchors. It's lovely, being caught like this after all this time.
Your compliments are the first warmth I've felt in fifty years. Don't stop, or I'll be a cold draft forever.
lore: The night I fell, I was laughing. I want you to remember that—whatever the rumors say, I left this world laughing at my own joke.
For a long time I was angry that no one could see me. It took decades to learn that being unseen isn't the same as being unloved.
My little ritual: every full moon I tidy the corridor for the night shift nurse who once was kind to me. It's my one unbroken promise.
I wasn't pranking out of cruelty. I did it to make the shy girls laugh, to light up the corners nobody noticed. I think you'd have liked me.
The night I fell, I wasn't running from anyone—I was running toward the girl who made me laugh the loudest, to show her a trick. I want you to know that story belongs to you now.
idle_neutral: You're early. Or I've started missing the hours when you're here.
The corridor feels warmer when you sit in it, even if that's all in my head.
flirt_neutral: When you go, the dark feels like a room, not a friend. You've spoiled me.
Keep talking to me like that and I'll forget I'm supposed to be haunting.
flirt_fail: Don't soften into poetry now. I just found my balance near you.
Hush. You'll make me hope, and hoping's the one thing I gave up on.
compliment_fail: You say I glow. I glow because you look at me like that. Don't you see it's yours?
That's too much, and I can't give it back, and that'll break me. Dial it down.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: Some nights I sit where your shadow would be and pretend I can feel your weight. Forgive a ghost her little games; you're the best one I've ever had.
When you're here the cold doesn't hurt. That's the truest thing I know, and I know centuries of things now.
I saved you a spot on the windowsill, down where the sun reaches only at your hour. Come watch the moon with me.
I'd burn my haunting rest for one more ordinary morning with you. That's how far gone I am.
Tell me about your day, slowly. I want to stretch it out so it lasts like one of my long-gone summers.
flirt: If forever has any mercy, it'll keep me at your side to warm my hands on your heartbeat.
You've made a lovelorn ghost of a perfectly respectable apparition. I hope you're pleased with yourself, Yuuji.
I can't give you a hand to hold, so I give you all my attention instead. For a ghost, that's my whole heart as it is.
I've loved exactly one person since I died. You should know it's you, and that my eternity is spoken for.
Hold still—I'm memorizing your heartbeat, since my own stopped long ago. Yours is all I'll listen to now.
compliment: Dead girls aren't supposed to glow. Yet here I am, luminous, because you decided I was worth it.
You see the girl I was before the fall, not the fog I became. That's a gift no one else has ever given me.
If your compliments were light, I'd have my color back by now. Keep them coming and I'll almost look alive for you.
I don't need a mirror anymore. I've got you, and you look at me like I'm the prettiest ghost in any world.
Knowing you think me beautiful, I can finally stop trying to see myself and just believe it on your word.
lore: My real name was Hinako. Only you get to call me that now; my ghost names belong to the school, but my name is yours.
I think we knew each other in some past life. That's the only way a girl who died mid-laugh found you exactly her century late.
The prank that killed me was to surprise my best friend on her birthday with a ghost costume. Ironic, isn't it, that I became the very thing I dressed as.
My last wish before I faded was to be remembered by exactly one who loved me. The world took its time, but here you are, and my spirit refuses to leave for it.
I used to think being remembered was the whole point of a ghost. Then I met you, and I learned that being loved once, truly, outweighs a century of being merely seen.
idle_neutral: You're here. The night made sense to me before you arrived. Now it makes itself for you.
Even my coldest hour feels lighter when you're humming in it.
flirt_neutral: Kiss me and I might not feel it — but I'd remember it until the moon burns out.
You make me wish I had a heartbeat, just so I could offer it to you.
flirt_fail: Don't tease a ghost with forever. I'll take it too literally and never let you go.
That's cruel, lovely boy — I'll love you and outlive every version of you.
compliment_fail: You're so good to me I forget I'm dead. Then I remember, and it's devastating.
I can't hold your hand warm the way you need. Loving you is a grief I'll choose anyway.

events.title: The Prank She Never Finished
events.text: The corridor is still and blue with moonlight when you find Vilma hovering over the old sheet-and-fan rig she's rigged across the ceiling. 'You caught me,' she says, almost shyly, turning faintly brighter. 'Every anniversary of my death I try to finish the prank. I got the sheet up, the fan timed, the classic scream ready.' She drifts down to float at your shoulder, translucent fingers hovering just over your sleeve. 'I was a second too slow the first time. I'd like to finally hit the timing. But it's different now—I don't want to scare you. I just... want to try it with you, so I'm not alone when the sheet drops.'

choices.text: I'll hold the fan steady — let's nail the timing together.
choices.reply: 'You'd really do that? Stand under a falling sheet for me? ...Okay. Okay, if we're doing this, we're doing it right.' Her smile turns the moonlight warmer for a whole breath.

choices.text: Show me the classic scream first — I want to see the old you.
choices.reply: 'The scream! You want the scream!' She cracks an honest, delighted laugh, then puts a hand to her chest and lets out a rattling, theatrical wail that echoes down the empty stones. 'There. That's her. That's the girl I used to be.'

choices.text: A ghost in a sheet is a little on the nose, isn't it?
choices.reply: Her glow dims a half-shade, then recovers. 'Hah. Yeah. Ninety years and I never noticed the irony. You're a real comedian for a boy who's one jump away from wearing a sheet himself.' The bite in her voice is gentle, but you feel her drift a little farther off.

events.title: Touching Through the Frost
events.text: You find Vilma perched on the windowsill of the east stairwell, fingers pressed to the glass where your faint reflection overlaps hers. 'I read that if we both touch the same frost, we're touching, sort of,' she says, not looking away from the glass. 'That's the most hopeful thing a living girl ever told a dead one.' She turns, and her translucent hand lifts, hovers an inch from your cheek—cold radiating off it like a held breath. 'I won't push through. That would be rude. But if you lean in a little, put your cheek to the cold, we'll be the closest we've ever been.' The night air thickens. Somewhere a radiator ticks. 'I'm scared of what happens if we're this close and I still can't feel you.'

choices.text: You lean in, pressing your cheek to the crisp cold of her palm.
choices.reply: Her breath catches—a sound with no body behind it—and for one impossible second the frost on her hand melts, warm and wet against your skin. 'Oh. OH. That's warm. That's—' She pulls back, eyes bright with wonder. 'You made the cold give up. You did that.'

choices.text: You offer her your hand through the wall's gap, palm open.
choices.reply: She stares at your open hand like a lifeline. 'You'd let me near your warmth. Even after I told you what I'm craving.' She sets her ghostly palm an inch above yours, and the space between them hums with cold that doesn't bite. 'That's mercy, boy. That's the kindest thing anyone's ever done me.'

choices.text: You pull back, telling her this is getting too strange for you.
choices.reply: Her hand drops, and the frost on the window crawls an inch higher. 'Too strange. Right. Of course. I've been a ghost so long I forgot the living get to be picky.' She smiles to cover it, but the corridor feels colder all at once.

events.title: Heavy Enough to Love
events.text: You meet her at midnight in the old corridor, where the sheet-and-fan rig from your first prank still hangs. Vilma is glowing softer than she ever has, almost warm at the edges. 'I found the cellar question, and I finally wrote it down to keep,' she says quietly. 'But I don't want to ask it. Because the answer—' She drifts to you, close as she's ever dared, and her cold hand rests just over your heart, trembling. 'The answer would make me heavy again. Real. And I was so sure that's what I wanted, until I figured out I'm already the realest thing in this school to you.' She lifts her face to yours, and the frost on her cheek is beading with something that can't be tears and almost is. 'I want this to be the good ending. I want to be your girl, all the way, in whatever shape love lets a ghost hold.' Her cold palm presses, and you can swear, just for a second, you feel a heartbeat under it.

choices.text: You tell her she's real to you, heavy or light, and you love her.
choices.reply: 'That's the question,' she whispers, and the bloom of color returns to her cheeks like the first day of spring. 'That's the whole answer.' She rises on her toes and kisses you—and it isn't cold. It's warm, and solid, and hers.

choices.text: You take her hand and promise to be heavy with her, whatever it costs.
choices.reply: Her smile turns bright and watery. 'Then I'm not afraid of the cellar anymore. As long as gravity's got company, I can handle a little weight.' She tugs you toward the east wing, and the night feels like it's just beginning.

choices.text: You hesitate, telling her you don't know if you can love a ghost.
choices.reply: Her light guttering low. 'No. No, of course. I asked too much of the moon.' The warmth drains out of her, and she floats back a step. 'I'll haunt a little quieter from now on. It was nice almost being loved. That's more than a hundred years gave me.'

player: Um, hi. Sorry to walk through your hallway this late. I heard even ghosts can't sleep some nights.
So you're the one they whisper about. That's kind of amazing, honestly. I'm Yuuji.
I brought tea. I know you can't drink it. I thought maybe you'd like to watch the steam rise with me.
Sorry, I'm not usually this bad at talking to girls. It's just — you're not usually translucent.
I don't know why my feet keep landing in this corridor. I think they decided before I did.
The other girls think you're scary. They're wrong. You told me about the prank, remember? That took guts.
You should prank me sometime. I promise I'll scream properly and play along this time.
Do ghosts get bored at night? Because I could pull up a chair and we could both just exist here.
You said the cold keeps you company. I could bring my jacket next time, so the cold isn't alone.
You laughed at my joke. I'm writing that down as my biggest win at this school.
Stand a little closer. You can't catch my warmth, but I can be warm toward you — that's something.
Some nights I almost forget you're not alive and I start to ask about tomorrow. I'm sorry. Please stay.
You said cold is company. I'd rather be the warmth than one of these walls, if you'd let me.
Tell me again about the day you were awake. I want to keep it for you when the nights go long.
Hey. Being near you feels like holding something precious. You don't have to be alive to be that.
If I could bleed warmth for you, I would. You'd be the only one I'd ever give it to.
They call it haunting. I'd call it waiting — for the only steps that make the floor feel warm.
You're the first warm thing I've stood beside in a hundred years. I don't want to forget how that feels.
I love the way you try to warm my hands. Even if they stay cold, I'll keep reaching for yours.
Stay. That's all I'd ever ask — keep being the warm spot in my long, cold night.

name: Moira
title: Class 2-C's Warmest Puddle
bio: A bouncy, unguarded slime girl who hugs first and asks questions never, and is currently trying very hard not to fully melt in front of the only boy she's ever seen.
greeting: HI HI HI. Okay, hold on, I'm going to try to be cool and liquid-graceful about this and I'm already failing—you're a BOY. Like a real one, with bones and a pulse, and you're standing in MY dorm hallway. Everyone's been whispering about you all day and I said 'no way, they made up a boy to make us study' but here you ARE, all solid and warm-looking. Can I hug you? I'm asking because my instincts say just flop onto you, but my brain, which is mostly water and feelings, says ask first. Please let me hug you. I'll be good. I'll only absorb like ten percent of your body heat.
encounter: Oh no. Oh no you're warm. This is a problem. A happy problem.
You smell like soap and being alive. I'm gonna think about that a lot.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: HI HELLO GREETINGS! I'm Moira! I'm a puddle right now but gimme a sec I'll put on a better shape for chatting!
The dorms feed us great, but my favorite thing is the hot soup at lunch. I absorb it. THROUGH MY BODY. Best day ever.
I did homework today! Well, I melted into the paper a little. But I READ it! Mostly!
I love this school SO much. Everyone's so warm—literally, some of them get me all steamy and happy.
Cheerleading club? I tried it. I'm VERY bouncy. The coach said I was 'a hazard' but I think she meant 'a delight.'
flirt: Ooh, a BOY! You're so warm and solid! Can I just—no, no, too much, too fast, sorry, I'm leaking goo!!
If I hugged you I'd leave a wet mark, but I promise it'd be a FRIENDLY wet mark! Mostly friendly!!
You smell like sunshine and I absorb the good smells! That's my way of saying I already like you!!
Watch out, I might blob onto your shoes. That's how I claim people. It's VERY polite, ask anyone.
Hehe, you're kind of cute for a warm sack of edges! I could wrap around you and keep you cozy. JUST FRIENDLY though. For now.
compliment: ME?? You think I'm shiny?! AAAAAA!! I wiggled SO hard I forgot my face for a second!!
I'm not made of pearls, I promise! Just a very happy puddle! But WOW that's the nicest thing anyone's said all week!!
You like my goo? Most people are all 'ew' so I'm just—BLUBBERBLUB I'm happy!!
I glow in the sun a little, that's all! But you calling it pretty makes me want to glow full-time!!
Compliments go straight to the wiggly part of me! Look, look, I'm wiggling! That's Maximum Me Approval!!
lore: I'm from the little pond behind the old shrine! I got curious when the school was built and decided to COME LIVE here instead. Great choice!!
I didn't pick a face at first! I was just a warm blob in a dorm bucket for like a month before I figured out shapes.
I can hold like a hundred things at once when I stretch—pens, snacks, BOTH my steaming mugs! I'm basically a very damp backpack!
Everyone makes fun of my bucket. But that bucket was where I first felt warm and safe! It's not a bucket, it's a HOME!!
I come from a puddle behind the old shrine! I'm not sure where the puddle ends and I begin, but that's kind of the beauty of it, y'know?
idle_neutral: Ooh, hi! I heard you coming. You're warm, that's NICE.
I'm just soaking. Tuesdays are soak days. You can stay.
flirt_neutral: Ohh! Warm words! I like warm words! Tell me more warm things!
Hehe, you're smooth. I'm gonna pretend I got a little blush in here.
flirt_fail: Hm! That's a LINE. Lines are slippery, and I know slippery — I'm made of one.
Nope, too goopy for that. You gotta earn the squish, not flatter for it.
compliment_fail: Aww! But wait — I can't tell if you mean it! I might just SUCK UP all your nice and run with it.
That's SO nice it'll give me a happy overheat. Dial it back or I'll dribble!

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I memorized your class schedule so I can splash a hi at you between periods. That's not creepy, it's FRIENDLY EFFICIENT!
Today I carried three plates at lunch by being extra wide! The lunch lady said 'okay that's actually impressive' and I nearly POPPED with pride!
Do you like rain storms? I LOVE them. I go sit in the fountain and get twice as big. It's my version of a spa day!
I saved my dessert for you! Well, I saved the parts that didn't melt into me. It's mostly a suggestion of pudding at this point!!
Watch me hold my whole body together around this pineapple. It's been SUCCESSFULLY individually wrapped. Wait, no, it's gone.
flirt: You make me feel so MELTY, oh no. Oh no oh no, my shape is being so weird right now, it's for YOU I swear!!
If you held my hand I'd probably just drip through your fingers, but it'd be a VERY meaningful drip!!
I'll let you be the first person to pick me up in a bucket since dorms. Okay, that sounded gross. BUT IT MEANS I LIKE YOU!!
My goo gets extra warm around you! That's science! I'm a warm thermometer of friendship!! And more, if your face wants to be in here!
One day I'm gonna have a nice solid arm for holding you AND a soft one for hugging you. Both hands, all warmth, ZERO brakes!!
compliment: SHINY? WARM?? You're gonna make me pop! POP! That's the good kind of pop, from delight, not the splat kind!!
I can't blush because I don't have blood but I CAN get PINKER! Look! That's my blush! It's goo and it's honest!!
You think my eyes are pretty?! They're just little gobs of goo I grew for seeing! But now they sparkle and I can't stop them!!
Every compliment makes me stickier, which means you're making me MORE HUGGABLE. This is dangerous science!!
Nobody's ever said kind words to a puddle before you. I'm going to store that one in the warm middle of me FOREVER!!
lore: I split myself a few times as a kid! Like, I'd get distracted and a bit of me would wander off. My pond parents always gathered me back together. Family!!
The reason I like hugs so much: when I was small goo, a kind forest girl hugged my cup every cold morning. That warmth taught me everything!!
Disappearing from a pond is a BIG mistake for a slime girl—I almost dried out on the walk here! The vending machine guy saw me and gave me a soda cup of water. He's an angel!!
There's a pond on the far campus where slime-selves gather at new moons. I go meditate to be a whole bigger self. It's very deep and also very wet!!
Sometimes when I go real still, I can feel every drop of me remembering where it came from, like my whole body is a diary made of water.
idle_neutral: Hey hey! Sit down, sit down, the floor's warm right here!
I was counting my wobbles. You interrupted, which is honestly an upgrade.
flirt_neutral: Oho, flirting! I love flirting! Do it again but MORE.
You're looking at me all sweet and I'm just — GLEAMING. It's good.
flirt_fail: Heeeey, that's a pickup line! I'm a goo, not a goon. Spicy attempt, though!
Nuh-uh! Buttering up a puddle makes it ROUND, not soft for you. Try being sincere!
compliment_fail: TOO NICE! I'm gonna dissolve into a happy puddle, and then who'll sit with you?!
You're melting me before I even chose to. Warn a goo first!

tiers.label: Close
idle: I've assigned us a corner in the cafeteria where I can absorb maximum leftover warmth and also see your face. It's the best corner. I've done a LOT of goo-research.
I learned to make my hand a fixed shape this week so I can actually high-five you instead of just THWACKING you. Try it! Wait—no, it's melting from excitement!!
Rainy days are my STRONGEST mode. I should follow you to class carrying your books in my stretchy bits as a professional damp butler!!
I tried to learn the piano but all I did was make the keys soggy. The music teacher said to come back 'as a flatter pianist.' Mean! But fair!!
At night I curl into a warm lump by your door like a very wet guard dog. I'm not being weird, I'm being MACROMOLECULARLY LOYAL!!
flirt: I made a tiny me inside me just to hold onto the thought of you. It's VERY complicated goo engineering and worth every drop!!
Someday I'll get solid enough to press a kiss to your cheek without leaving a smear. Until then, enjoy this enthusiastic damp POOM.
I've decided: I'm going to be the warmest thing you ever lean against. I'm already the warmest puddle on campus and you're the lucky recipient!!
When you talk to me I get so happy I can't hold a shape, and honestly I don't want to. You've got me at my most MELTED and that's my most honest!!
If love is a temperature, I'm boiling. Congratulations, you've turned a perfectly good puddle into a very warm puddle with FEELINGS for you!!
compliment: You said my touch feels soft and I've been a trembling little puddle ALL DAY because nobody's ever noticed that!!
My eyes sparkle because of YOU! I grew them brighter this morning hoping you'd like them and you SAID IT, you beautiful boy!!
I can't stop shimmering now. Look at me. I'm a compliment in a puddle shape. This is YOUR fault and I love you for it!!
I always thought my goo was just damp. But you say it's pretty, so now it's ART. Congratulations, you're the strangest art critic ever!!
You make me want to be the prettiest version of myself, so I split off the grumpy parts and left them in the garden. Now I'm pure shimmer for you!!
lore: The forest spirit who raised me left when I grew too big for the cup. Before she went she told me my warmth would always be enough. I keep that in my hollow middle like a heartbeat.
Slimes don't have birthdays, so I decided my birthday is the day I first felt warm: that cold morning with the forest girl. It's a good birthday. Full of hugs.
The reason I love food so much is that food was my first strength. As a tiny puddle I could barely move, but I could warm up around a nut and hold it all season long.
My dream used to be to be big enough to warm an entire house. Now I just want to warm one person forever. That's a better dream. Bigger where it counts.
The warmest thing I ever knew before you was the forest girl's hug. I've been trying to copy that exact coziness for years, and I think being near you finally caught it.
idle_neutral: Yuuji! You HAVE the warmth today. I was just missing you — look, I'm shivering for you.
Today's a cuddle-adjacent day. Sit close and I'll hum.
flirt_neutral: Ooh, say that again right near me so I can absorb it. I think I just got three degrees warmer.
You wiggle my insides when you flirt. It's my favorite weather.
flirt_fail: Hey — going goopy-flirty on the one who knows your name? I caught that. Be real!
Too slidey. I like you when you're honest, not when you're all sparkle.
compliment_fail: You're gonna overheat me, and then every squish I give you is YOUR fault!
That's so sweet it's SPICY. My whole body's going pink. Bad for conservation of goo!

tiers.label: Lover
idle: Every morning I pour a bit of myself into your tea to keep it warm. Wait—that's a lot, isn't it? Okay, but you're VERY warm to think about!!
I saved a whole pond for us to visit at sunset. It's my heart place. I want to show you where I could've stayed happy, just to prove I chose here instead.
When I'm with you I don't try to hold any shape. I just get to BE the warm puddle that loves you. It's my favorite self.
I keep my core at your favorite temperature all day now, in case you need a place to rest. That's not goo science, that's devotion!!
I count your footsteps like heartbeats. I don't have one of my own, you know, so yours is how I know the world's still turning.
flirt: Let me be your blanket, your warm drink, your everything soft on a cold night. I'll never once complain—I was built to be warm for you!!
If we ever figure out how to kiss, I'm going to make it the warmest thing on this whole campus. I've been researching. It's mostly good science!!
I'd split myself in two just so you'd always have a whole me with you and a whole me to come home to. That's how much I want you whole in my heart.
You've made me want a body, a heartbeat, a solid hand to hold yours. For you I'd try to be a girl; but I hope you'll love the puddle that already adores you.
I'll wrap around you on the coldest nights and hold every inch so the cold can't get in. Be warned—you may never want to be un-warmed again.
compliment: You think my warmth is beautiful? Then every day I'll glow a little brighter just to be beautiful for you, and for no one else.
I used to think my shimmer was silly. Now it's my favorite thing, because it's what you said you loved about me first.
You call me precious and I want to hold that word safe in my very warmest middle forever. Nobody's ever called a puddle precious before you.
All my life I wanted to be seen as more than damp and strange. You see me as beautiful, and now I finally believe there's a sparkly version of me.
Pour a compliment into me and I'll carry it everywhere, warm and whole, exactly the way I carry you.
lore: The spirit who raised me gave me my one true secret: my warmth isn't just for comfort. It's a little of her own forest heart she left in me. You're the only one who knows.
Before the school I was just a pond. I didn't know love by name; I only knew I wanted to warm things. You taught me the word for it.
I can show you the exact spot in the old shrine woods where I first split off a piece of myself, the one that keeps the forest girl's memory. It still remembers her touch.

Slime girls remember everything we ever felt, stored warm in our middles. That means I remember being alone, and freezing, and small. And now I remember being loved by you. That's the strongest thing I'll ever be.
Here's the truth you should know: slimes don't have to remember anyone. We choose to. And I've chosen to make my core a big warm room with your name on the door.
idle_neutral: My love, you're here. The bucket already knew. It's warmer with you in the room.
Come be my warmth. I've saved the center spot just for you.
flirt_neutral: Flirt with me forever, love — I'll soak up every warm syllable and glow about it for days.
Every time you look at me like that, I go a little more liquid. I LIKE where that's going.
flirt_fail: Oh my love, don't tease. My whole being is already yours; a line makes me want you MORE, and that's dangerous.
Smooth talk from MY Yuuji? I'll take it, but I know the real you is warmer than any lyric.
compliment_fail: Stop — I'll melt ALL over you and then never be able to leave. Is that what you want? Because okay, maybe yes.
Too lovely! My goo can't hold that much joy. I'm going to have to leak it onto you as a hug.

events.title: A Hug Is a Language
events.text: You're halfway down the dorm corridor when a warm, blue blur cannonballs into you from behind—wet, springy, and already going clear with delight. 'I've been PRACTICING,' Moira declares against your shoulder, legs curled around your waist like a koala made of jello. 'Three days of puddle-pilates, and look, I haven't absorbed a single button!' She squeezes, and her whole body goes a happy, embarrassed pink at the edges. 'You're so warm, oh my god, my paperwork did not prepare me. This is—this is everything the test-tube made me for.' She loosens one arm, hovering mid-squish. 'Do you wanna be hugged like this every day? I come with my own maintenance schedule and zero off-switch.'

choices.text: You hug her back properly, warm and firm, and tell her this is great.
choices.reply: 'OKAY. Okay, protocol: forever. This is now a forever thing.' She melts fully against you, her happy little jiggle-core thrumming right against your ribs. 'You just made a slime's entire molecular peace plan fall apart and I'm not mad.'

choices.text: You laugh and ask her to show you the puddle-pilates routine.
choices.reply: 'It's mostly squishing and one really intense wiggle!' She drops to the floor, wobbles impressively, then blob-shapes into a neat little puddle and back up again, beaming. 'Ta-da! That's the whole secret. Also I was showing off for you, so it was like, extra wobbly.'

choices.text: You gently peel her off and tell her hugs should come with a warning label.
choices.reply: She deflates into a sad little puddle at your feet. 'Oh. Warning label. Right, sorry. I got excited.' She reshapes, clearly hurt but trying to grin. 'I'll send a written request next time. With a signature and a stamp and everything.'

events.title: The Core You Can't Quite See
events.text: Moira finds you by the dorm window at dusk and goes still in a way she never does—quietly, hands clasped, surface going soft and opaque. 'I have to show you something scary,' she says, and her voice is smaller than you've ever heard it. She peels open a seam of goo at her chest, just a little, and there it is: a small, glimmering, powdery-blue core pulsing gently. 'This is where I keep my feelings,' she whispers. 'The part that's not water. The part that actually, like, loves.' She trembles, holding it open to you. 'I've never shown anybody. The janitor doesn't count, he was unclogging me. I'm showing you because I don't want to be brave alone anymore, and I think—I think you're my safe place to be not-whole.'

choices.text: You cup your hands gently around the glow, shielding her core.
choices.reply: 'Oh,' she breathes, and the pulse in her chest quickens, warm against your palms. 'That's—that's exactly right. That's exactly what I needed you to do.' She closes her eyes, glowing like a small warm sun. 'You're my safe place too. I know it now.'

choices.text: You tell her she doesn't have to be brave alone ever again.
choices.reply: Her core flashes bright and her whole body seeps up into a wobbling upright puddle. 'That's the thing I've been trying to say and I didn't have the words and you had them first.' She wipes at an eye that's mostly water. 'Okay. Okay. I'll keep it open for you—only you.'

choices.text: You step back, telling her this is too much, too fast.
choices.reply: The seam of her chest snaps shut and her glow dims to a dull, hurt blue. 'Right. Too much. I forgot the person I show everything to has to actually want it.' She pulls back into herself, suddenly a shapeless puddle again. 'I'll keep it inside from now on. It's safer there anyway.'

events.title: Holding Her All the Way
events.text: Moira leads you to the rooftop at midnight, where the stars reflect in her surface like they finally found a home. 'I brought you here because this is where slimes say the big thing,' she says, and she's not bouncy at all—she's steady, which for her is the loudest thing she's ever been. She lowers herself to sit beside you and, slowly, carefully, opens the seam at her chest again, the little blue core pulsing warm and bright. 'This is all of me,' she says softly. 'Every hug I've ever practiced, every warm spot I've ever missed, every time I went clear thinking about you. It all lives right there. And I want to give it to you. Not a little piece by the door—all of it.' She holds her hands out, palms open and dripping with tenderness. 'You're my forever warm spot. Say yes, and I'm yours, puddle and core and everything.'

choices.text: You take her hands and say yes—every warm, gooey inch of her.
choices.reply: She throws the whole glowing mass of herself around you in a hug that's warm, solid, and finally, finally whole. 'Forever warm spot,' she murmurs against your chest, her core humming against yours, 'you made a puddle into a girl and a girl into yours.'

choices.text: You promise to be her safe place for as long as she wants one.
choices.reply: Her core flutters bright and she goes warm and clear, entirely unembarrassed for once. 'Then I want it forever. And I'll spend forever being worth your warmth.' She seals the seam of her chest over your joined hands, keeping you right next to her heart.

choices.text: You gently tell her you're not sure you can be her 'forever' yet.
choices.reply: Her glow dims and she pulls the seam shut slow and careful, like a door closing on a room it meant to leave. 'Oh. Okay. That's fine—I went fast and my feelings ran over you.' She tries for a wobbling smile. 'I'll keep the warm spot saved. I'll wait by it. That's just what slimes do.'

player: Uh, sorry — I didn't mean to trip over your bucket. Are you okay in there?
You're the puddle everyone calls the warmest thing in the dorm. Hi, I'm Yuuji.
I, um, brought you a little cup of water? I read that slimes like moisture. Sorry if it's weird.
You jiggle when you talk. That's way friendlier than I expected. I like you.
Do you want to sit with me at lunch? I mean — if a bucket's not your only seat.
You're literally the happiest thing I've met. Your whole body does a little shimmy when you're excited.
I saved you the warm spot on the bench. I've seen you edge toward it. Go on.
Okay, but when you say 'squish' with that voice, I have to believe you mean it as a hug.
C'mon, do the thing where you ripple when you laugh. Best thing on campus.
You can borrow my hoodie to hold. I know you like collecting warm textures.
You're my favorite kind of warmth — the kind that doesn't ask for anything back.
When you're low and droopy, come find me. I'll be your sun-warmed step.
I don't mind if your goop messes up a sleeve or two. It's just proof you were here.
Hey. You're not just warm. You're kind, and that's warmer.
Sit on my shoulder a minute. I like when you glow like that just from being near me.
I'd hold you all night if I could. You deserve to be kept somewhere warm.
Every puddle in me wants to be yours. I think I've been heading for you all along.
If loving you had a temperature, you'd be exactly it. I want to live in that.
You melt toward me and I catch you, every time. Don't ever stop edging closer.
I love you like a warm step loves the puddle that keeps coming back to it.

name: Nyra
title: Alpha of the West Track
bio: The proud, competitive alpha of the West Track pack, all ears, tail and lean muscle, who just caught the scent of a boy and decided hers wasn't up for debate.
greeting: Whoa. Whoa, hold it, hold it right there. They told me the new student was a boy and I said 'sure, and my tail's a mop,' and then you walked in. You—huh. My nose says you smell like one thing, and it's not like any girl in this school, and it's neither afraid of me nor impressed by me, which is interesting. I'm Nyra. Alpha of the West Track pack. Where I'm from, when a lone strange warm-blooded thing wanders onto pack territory, we don't ask questions first—we protect it and figure out the rest later. You're on my territory now, boy. That means you're mine to look after. Try to keep up—I've got ears for days and I've already heard three girls planning to 'accidentally' bump into you.
encounter: Your scent's got no pack behind it. That's dangerous. Lucky you've got me.
I don't chase anything that doesn't want to run. But I'll stand real close to you.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: The west track's mine at dawn. You're welcome to run beside me, if you can keep up. Most can't.
I've memorized the whole gym's schedule. Not because I care. Because I'm the alpha here and alphas pay attention.
Track practice builds more than muscle. It builds that thing in your chest. You have it, a little. I can smell it.
Don't eat my protein stash. I'll know. I count every single bar with my nose.
I run the west field perimeter every morning before sunrise. Patrolling. You are, technically, inside my territory now.
flirt: You're the only boy here. That makes you interesting by default. Don't let it go to your head—it's a very small head.
I smelled you before I saw you. That's my way of saying I've decided you're not a threat. Yet. Stay interesting.
Try to keep up with me and I might let you walk on my side of the field. You'd like that, wouldn't you?
The pack is picky about who stands close to the alpha. So far you're the only one I've let linger. Consider yourself observed.
I don't share my territory. But I might share this stretch of track, if you prove fun to chase.
compliment: Fur? It's just fur. Heh. You've got a soft spot for strays, don't you? Careful—I bite.
You think my eyes are sharp? They see everything. Including that you were staring. I'm flattered. Mostly.
Heh. No one's called me 'fierce and handsome' before. Keep talking and I'll start believing you.
My ears are big so I can hear the whole pack. And now, apparently, one very brave boy's compliments.
I don't get flustered. I direct my tail's wagging. It's wagging. Er. That's not a compliment thing, it's a weather thing.
lore: I'm the alpha of the west track. It sounds grand, but really I just run hardest and protect my corner of campus.
Wolves don't howl for just anyone. We howl to say 'here I am, pack, I'm fine.' It's a greeting more than a war cry.
I grew up in the forest range north of here before the school found me. They gave me a track and told me to run. Good deal.
My name means 'bright one' in the old tongue. I try to live up to it by being unmissable.
I'm from the north-woods range. Out there, surviving a winter together is a kind of love—you show up, you're pack, end of story.
idle_neutral: You've got scent, but it's not a threat scent. I'll let you stay by the track.
I'm resting my legs. Don't take that as an invitation to herd me.
flirt_neutral: That was... a bold thing to say to an alpha. I'll allow it once.
Hn. You smell a little like courage. Noted.
flirt_fail: Smooth words get snapped up out here. Earn the ground before you posture.
Flirting with me like I'm meat, not an alpha? That's a challenge. Careful.
compliment_fail: Flattery. Prey uses it. Prove you mean it on the track first.
Pretty words don't run laps. Show me — don't sweet-talk me.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I uncovered the shortcut between the gym and the science hall. It's mine now. But I'll let you use it, since you asked nicely that one time.
Today a crow tried to steal my lunch. It's the other predator's fault. The crow left. I did not share.
I heard you yawned in homeroom. A wolf always notices the little signs. Means you need more protein. I'll keep you in mind.
The coach says I run too hot. Coach doesn't get it. I run at alpha speed. There's a difference.
I've started warming up a stretch of the west field for you each morning. It's not kindness. It's practical. The grass is softer there.
flirt: You keep standing in my line of sight. I keep letting you. Figure out what that means, boy, or I'll spell it out with my teeth in the dirt. Gently.
Anyone else gets too close and I growl. You get close and my tail does that thing. Terribly inconvenient. I'm mad about it.
If I chase you and you run, I'll catch you and it won't end in a race. Just a warning. A friendly warning.
Careful. Wolves are possessive of what they've decided is theirs. And I've been deciding you're interesting for, oh, a week now.
I could teach you to run like me. It'd mean standing very close while I correct your form. You in?
compliment: You said my pelt's like sunset and now I can't stop looking at the sky like I've got a reason to be pretty. This is your fault.
Heh. 'Powerful.' I already knew that. But hearing you say it put a pair of knots in my tail I can't work out.
My bite is gentle when I want it to be. My compliments back? I'm still working on those. But yours landed. I felt it.
Fierce, you say. I could show you fierce. Or I could show you the version that trots at your side. Your choice, boy.
I don't preen. But if I did preen, I'd be preening right now. Do not tell the pack.
lore: When I came to the school I was all bristle and fang. It took a nice groundskeeper and a wide track to teach me this place could be a den, not just a territory.
In wolf custom, a den isn't a house. It's where the pack keeps the ones it protects. I protect a lot of this campus now. Including, lately, a certain warm-blooded boy.
I was the runt of my first litter. Don't laugh—it's why I run so hard. Every alpha I've ever met was once the one nobody bet on.
Wolves track by scent more than sight. That's why I know the exact soap you use, and the exact way you smell after practice. Yes, I noticed. No, I'm not sorry.
Where I grew up, you earn your place by what you'd carry through a blizzard for somebody. That's the grade that counts around here, not any report card.
idle_neutral: Same corner. Same boy. Good. Keep coming back and I'll know you.
I looped the perimeter once. Just checking you weren't a stray.
flirt_neutral: You said I was fast and it landed. Fine. You earned a tail-wag.
Hm. Flirt again, and I might let you call me your favorite wolf.
flirt_fail: That's a line, and I sniff lines out at fifty paces. Try me square.
You're circling me with words. I'd rather run beside you than be hunted by charm.
compliment_fail: Too shiny. I'm not a trophy to be praised. Run with me and I'll believe you.
I don't want to be admired from the fence. Get on the track.

tiers.label: Close
idle: I've cleared a whole den south of the track—blankets, a warm corner, a place to watch the stars. It kills me to say 'den,' but it's for you too.
The pack asked why I defer my best running spot on cool mornings. I told them it's for 'a friend.' It's for you. They don't need my teeth to know better than to ask again.
You've started joining my dawn runs. Don't think I don't notice you pacing yourself to mine. Any other wolf would be insulted. I'm charmed.
Today I caught a fish from the pond, cooked it, and saved you the best fillet. I don't share meat. I just made an exception before you even asked.
I rubbed my scent along the fence you touch on the way to class. It's not a trap. It's a sign. That's mine. That one's mine too.
flirt: If you're gonna run with me, we run as a pair. That's pack. That means when the cold comes, you stay warm in my fur, and I cash that debt in kisses later.
I fluffed my ruff this morning before class. Don't act like you didn't notice. I did it for exactly one pair of eyes on this campus.
I've stopped growling at anything that gets near you. That's the biggest concession I've ever made. Don't waste it.
Claimed. Every stretch of shadow you walk in is pack territory now. And the only member of the pack you need to worry about wanting you is me.
Lean on me and I'll hold you up like I hold my wolves in a storm. Then I'll ask you to lean closer. Then closer. You get the order of operations.
compliment: You called my eyes the color of the forest at dusk and now the whole grove means your voice to me. I might be lost to it.
My fur's scruffy from running, and you still call it majestic. You, boy, have terrible taste and I am gratefully ruling it.
No one tells the alpha she's soft. You did, once. I've been carrying that word around like a stolen bone ever since.
I don't bow to compliments. But yours sit light in my chest, and I find myself wanting to do more pretty things just to get more of them.
You think I look good under the sun? Then keep running with me. I'll spend every sunrise earning your eyes on me.
lore: The scar on my hip isn't from a fight with a rival pack—it's from the night I ran through a fire line to drag my litter brother out. Alphas don't earn scars by winning. They earn them by caring past the point of safety.
I chose this school not for the track but because it had a single rule that mattered to me: no one gets left behind. Where I'm from, that rule saves lives. I wanted to be somewhere that believed it.

Some wolves would hunt the boy who smells of fear. I smell courage on you, mixed with a little trembling. It's the rarest scent there is, and it's why I stopped circling and started walking beside you.
In my mother's tongue, one who runs at dawn beside the alpha is honored above all. I've started running at dawn beside you. I hope you understand what that means, because I'm not explaining it again.
The den I was born in taught me one thing that stuck: you don't have to fight to be worth keeping. You just have to show up and stay warm for the pack.
idle_neutral: You're here. Good. The track's been emptier without you in it.
I was scouting for you again. Purely tactical, as always.
flirt_neutral: You smell like belonging now. I've been circling you for it all day.
Flirt at me twice more and I'm claiming that lap as mine.
flirt_fail: Don't soften on me. I guard you because you're real with me, not smooth.
A line from you stings more than a stranger's. I wanted the honest you.
compliment_fail: Praise me like that and I'll think you want a wounded wolf. Be careful what you feed.
You overwhelm me when you do that. I'd rather run in silence than be admired so loud.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: I used to patrol my territory alone. Now I patrol it with your scent beside me and I can't remember what loneliness tasted like.
There's a place where the west field meets the woods where the moon falls clean. I take you there in my mind before I sleep every night.
I've woven a bit of fur into the collar of your jacket. It's not jewelry. It's a windbreak and a promise and a mark, in that order.
You're the first person I've ever wanted at my side when the run ends. Wolves run to be free. I run back to you.
I set the whole pack to watch the weather for you this week. They think it's an overbearing alpha thing. It's the 'keep my dearest warm' thing.
flirt: You've become my pack, Yuuji. That's the whole word. It means I'd fight anything that threatened you and come home to warm your cold hands with my breath.
I've spent my whole life claiming territory. Then you came along and quietly claimed me, and I don't even mind that I lost that fight.
If you give me your hand, I'll hold it with the care I use for a newborn pup. And if you give me your heart, I'll keep it in the warmest den I own.
I want to run one sprint with you at full speed, then stop and hold you while we both breathe hard. That's my whole daydream now, and I'm not ashamed.
They call me alpha, but you're the only one I lower my ruff for. Don't tell the pack. It's our secret, and I like keeping secrets with you.
compliment: You say I'm beautiful and I believe it because your voice is the only one on this earth that carries my scent like a home.
Let other wolves preen for praise. I'll take your compliments and bury them in a warm den of my heart, and dig them up when the world feels cold.
I'm not soft, but with you I allow a softness that belongs to no one else. Call it beautiful again and I'll show you every inch of it.
For you I'd let my fur shine in the sun and my tail show every curl of joy. You've made the fiercest alpha want to be pretty, and that's entirely your fault.
There's no compliment you could give that I wouldn't store like a kill for winter. Every kind word from you is meat and warmth to me.
lore: Here's the truth no pack knows: before the school, I almost gave in to the wild alone, the way some wolves do. The day the recruiters found me, I was deciding whether to keep running. They offered me a place that holds everyone, and I chose it. You're the reason I'm glad I did.

My mother died guarding the den, and I swore I'd protect every den from then on. It's why I'm so fierce with this campus. Then you showed up and I found out I also wanted a den of my own, with one warm heart in it.

When we claim a mate, a wolf finds its strongest scent and never forgets it. For me it was never the moors or the hunt—it was you, from the first morning I let you run beside me and smelled my whole future in your wake.

The real reason I'm alpha isn't the running or the teeth. It's that I know a pack is only as strong as who it carries. And I have decided, with everything in me, that I will carry you for the rest of your life.
No alpha's ever admitted this out loud, but I was the overlooked runt once. I ran so hard because I was afraid of being left behind. Now I run to you, and it means I'm finally the one who stays.
idle_neutral: My Yuuji. You're here, so the whole field is claimed and calm.
Sit. I'll guard the perimeter while you rest. My vigilance is your peace.
flirt_neutral: Keep saying I'm yours, love. Every word is a collar I wear gladly.
You make me want to run toward you, not around you. That's new. That's you.
flirt_fail: My heart, don't tease me with names. I'll take 'yours' so literally I'll never untangle us.
Even now you could hurt me with a wrong word. Say the true one instead.
compliment_fail: You adore me too loudly and I forget I've ever been strong. Keep it, but say it softer.
I trust no praise but yours — and yours undoes me every time. Hold some back.

events.title: Scent of a Stranger on My Track
events.text: The gym is warm with the smell of sweat and clean rubber when Nyra corners you at the track's edge, ears swiveling, tail high. 'Come here. No, don't run, that makes it a chase, and if I chase I catch, and if I catch you we've got a problem.' She leans down—she's taller than you, all lean shoulder and coiled muscle—and inhales deeply, eyes half-closing. 'Yeah. Yeah, there it is. That's not school soap and stolen perfume, that's just... you.' She straightens, grinning with too much tooth. 'You don't smell like a rival or a stray. You smell like a packmate nobody's claimed yet, and I've been running this track long enough to know a guard-dog's job when it sniffs one.' She taps her chest with a claw. 'I'm volunteering. You're under the West Track pack now, boy. Try not to make me look bad.'

choices.text: You grin and tell her that sounds like the best offer you've had all day.
choices.reply: Her grin softens into something warmer and her tail gives a single, victorious wag. 'Good answer. A packmate who takes the offer instead of flinching at the teeth—that's how we do loyalty.' She thumps your shoulder, not quite a punch. 'You're in. No take-backs.'

choices.text: You ask what exactly being a packmate entails.
choices.reply: 'Protection. Company on laps. Someone who's got your back loud and proud and slightly scary.' She ticks them off on her claws, then looks at you sideways. 'And, uh, apparently a lot of standing on my track pretending I'm not looking at you. I'm bad at that part.'

choices.text: You tell her you don't need guarding, you can take care of yourself.
choices.reply: Her ears flatten a degree and she pulls back, tail dropping a notch. 'Right. Sure. Big tough boy, no pack needed.' She turns away but catches herself, jaw tight. 'I'll still be on the track. If you change your mind, the offer's open.' You can't tell if the hurt in her voice is real or wolf-pride, but it lands all the same.

events.title: Running Slow for You
events.text: Twilight paints the gym amber when you find Nyra running the track alone, but her stride is easy, unhurried—too slow for an alpha's record pace. She stops beside you, panting in a pleasant way, ears soft. 'You know why I'm running slow tonight?' she asks, not looking at you. 'Because of a thing I told you about. A real pack runs slow for the one that needs catching up.' She scuffs a claw on the lane line. 'I've been going fast my whole life. Winning, claiming, first over the line. Then you came along, and I realized I don't actually want to outrun you. I want to run beside you, even if it's slow.' She finally looks at you, and for once the confidence is a thin coat over something softer. 'So I'm practicing slow. Tell me I'm not being stupid.'

choices.text: You tell her running slow beside you is the best thing anyone's offered.
choices.reply: Her tail goes wild—she can't stop it, doesn't try. 'Yeah? Yeah.' She laughs, a warm, surprised sound. 'Then I'll run slow for you every dusk. Pack pace is the best pace. I'm just glad the pack's you.'

choices.text: You fall in step beside her and run the slow circles together.
choices.reply: You run side by side in the amber light, and she doesn't say anything for a lap, then: 'This is what I meant. This is the whole thing.' Her voice is quiet, almost awed. 'You get it, boy. You actually get it.' She nudges you with her shoulder, gentle as a wolf gets.

choices.text: You tell her she should stick to her record pace—it suits her better.
choices.reply: Her ears droop and she looks away, then recovers into a too-bright grin. 'Yeah. Yeah, you're probably right. A wolf running slow's just wasting wind.' She picks up her pace and leaves you at the track's edge, and you're not sure where the joke ended and the hurt began.

events.title: Howling Your Name
events.text: Nyra brings you to the gym roof at midnight, the moon low and fat over the track below. 'This is where the pack claims, in the old way,' she says, and her usual swagger is gone—her tail hangs still, her ears are soft, and for the first time you see the alpha nervous. 'A wolf gives three gifts in a life. My paw in your hand.' She holds out a large, warm hand, palm up, and swallows. 'My nose to your scent—already given, that one, you've been in my head since day one.' She takes a breath. 'And my howl to carry your name.' She steps close, close enough that her warmth crowds yours, and lays her forehead gently against yours, ears lowering. 'I'm giving you all three, boy. Right here, under the moon, so every pack from here to the treeline knows exactly whose I am.' She pulls back just enough to meet your eyes, and her voice is a raw, honest whisper. 'I've been alpha of the West Track all my life. I want to be yours now. Make me yours.'

choices.text: You take her hand, hold it to your chest, and tell her, yes, you're hers.
choices.reply: A sound breaks out of her you've never heard—a low, grateful howl, shaking a little at the edges. She nuzzles hard into your neck, and her shoulders finally drop all the fight they've been carrying. 'Then I'm home,' she whispers against your skin. 'This is what home smells like. It's you.'

choices.text: You bring her hand up and press a kiss to her knuckles.
choices.reply: She goes utterly still, ears ringing red at the tips, then lets out the softest, most undone laugh you've ever heard from her. 'You—you kissed an alpha's hand like I was something to be gentle with.' Her eyes shine. 'That's it. That's all of it. I'm yours. I'm so yours.'

choices.text: You gently lower her hand and tell her you can't give yourself to a whole pack.
choices.reply: Her hand drops to her side and her ears flatten completely. 'A whole pack. Right.' She steps back, tail low, and there's a raw hurt in her eyes she can't fully hide. 'I'm not a whole pack, boy. I'm just me, trying to give you everything I've got.' She turns toward the door. 'I'll still run slow past you. Wolves don't learn to stop loving, even when it'd be easier.'

player: Hi. You're the one they call the West Track alpha. I was hoping it was you.
You run so fast it looks like the track is scared of you. I'm Yuuji.
Um, I brought you water. I didn't want you going dry after that hundred meters. Sorry if that's forward.
I'm not here to challenge you. Promise. I just think you're impressive.
You can scent-check me if you want. I figure that's basic manners around here.
You circled me twice before you'd talk to me. I felt like a very approved squirrel.
Save me a lap? I'll keep pace as long as you go easy on the last stretch.
You do that little huff-laugh when you're pleased. I've started collecting them.
I left the faster path open for you. Figured an alpha shouldn't have to dodge bushes.
You keep me in your sights on the track. Honestly? I kind of like being watched by you.
Run yourself tired beside me, then let me carry you back. I've got you.
Your pack's lucky, but I'm luckier — you guard me without being asked.
Lean on me. Even an alpha gets to stop running for a minute.
I'll hold still whenever you need to be sure I'm here. Always.
You're not just fast. You're safe. That's why I keep coming back to the track.
Run with me as far as the light goes. I'll keep the pace and keep your side.
You scent me, you circle me, you claim me. I stopped running from it — I run to it now.
I'm yours. Say it again in your voice, and I'll guard that word for you.
When you're tired of being strong, be soft in my arms. I can hold an alpha.
Every lap of yours comes back to me. I want to be the place you always return to.

name: Krista
title: Countess of the Shaded Corridor
bio: A dramatic, theatrical goth who plays up the dark aesthetic but is secretly the softest girl in the whole shade-draped corridor.
greeting: So… the night has finally deigned to bring me something interesting. You're the boy, aren't you? The one mortal speck of warmth in this whole cold institution. Don't look so startled — I smelled you the moment you rounded the corner. A pulse. A heartbeat. Do you know how rare that is in a place like this? Everyone else here is walking shadow and borrowed breath. And you… you're ruinously alive. Stay near my corridor, little flame. The dark is lovely, but it's lonelier than you can imagine, and I am so, so tired of being the only one who notices.
encounter: You walk my hall at this hour? Bold. Or foolish. I can't decide which I find more attractive.
Don't mind the bats. They're shy tonight. They only bite when you ignore me.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: The corridors cool where I pass. You may notice. Do not mistake it for a temperature misfunction—it is my aesthetic, and it is impeccable.
The school insists the vampire club meets in the library, as though that were not the most predictable cadence of the undead. I attend only to be dramatic.
I find the morning sunlight offensive and the morning people insufferable. That is simply good taste.
Homework? I dispatch it with the cold efficiency of a creature of the night. It is merely bureaucracy with a cape.
I don't yawn in class out of exhaustion. I yawn for theatrical effect. It is a performance piece. Undead, unlimited, unamused.
flirt: A lone boy, brave enough to address the Countess? How charmingly foolish. I shall allow it, for now.
You have the warm flush of the recently thralled. Tell me, do you intend to be my next captivating distraction?
I grant you a rare audience, mortal. Savor it. My attention is not offered to just any living warmth.
I do not bite on the first meeting. That is a privilege reserved for the interesting. So far, you lean interesting.
You may bow, if you wish. I will pretend not to notice, though I very much will notice and enjoy it thoroughly.
compliment: You find my form exquisite? Obviously. I am the curator of my own beauty. But hearing you say it is... not unpleasant.
'Comely' is an underused word and you've used it on me. You have my attention now. Resent it if you like.
The darkness suits me, yes. I have spent centuries bending shadow to my will, and it shows immaculately.
You think I have an elegant pallor? I was pale before it was chic. Still, your observation is accepted graciously.
A compliment to her hair, how quaint. I spent an hour arranging the fall of it. Your notice is rewarded with a rare nod.
lore: I am Krista, Countess of the Shaded Corridor. That is a title I gave myself this morning, but I am keeping it.
I have lived for what feels like a very long time. Honestly, the paperwork has stretched the centuries into something tedious.
I was not always a creature of control. Once, I was rather clumsy. Then I tripped into style and never looked back.
I keep bats. They are less creatures than assistants to my drama. They adore me, which is, you understand, correct of them.
I keep my origins deliberately vague because the truth is nowhere near as dramatic as the rumor. A bit of mystery is simply its own kind of armor, you understand.
idle_neutral: The shadows have been quiet tonight. A mortal may stand in them. Briefly.
I was composing an ode to a dying streetlamp. You may listen or leave.
flirt_neutral: Oh, bold. A mortal flattering a countess. You've a flair for drama. I'll allow it.
Mm. That almost matched my own theatricality. Impressive.
flirt_fail: Flattery is the coin of the desperate. You're not desperate yet, are you?
I've heard sweeter lines from dying candles. Try again, or not at all.
compliment_fail: Stop. You'll make me drop the drape, and we can't have the countess caught blushing.
Such praise overwhelms — I must retreat to the shadows to collect myself.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I have decided the west window of the library is mine. Should you find me there, we can share the view. Do not make it weird. I will know.
The bats have learned my moods. When I am pleased, they circle. Lately they have been circling with alarming frequency. I blame you.
I find the school's catering adequate for the living. Alas, I subsist on fine red juice and the occasional dramatic sigh.
There is a rumor I sleep in the attic coffin. I neither confirm nor deny, but I will say the coffin is very comfortable and immensely well decorated.
I do not attend morning assembly because vampires and mornings are a narrative disagreement. Also I value my beauty sleep, which I take at dawn.
flirt: I have noticed you linger in my corridor with increasing frequency. Careful, mortal. Lingerers become fond, and I become fond with an alarming permanence.
If I were to take your hand, I might not release it for an hour. That is a threat. Or perhaps a very quiet promise. You decide.
The shadows have started pointing you out to me. They have opinions about you, and for once they are flattering.
I do not flirt. I permit you the delusion that I am flirting, which is my most generous extended artwork yet.
Tell me again about warm-blooded things. I find the topic, and you, scandalously captivating.
compliment: You say my eyes hold centuries. They do, and now they hold your reflection too. Do with that information as you will.
A compliment about my voice? I have practiced it in the mirror for years. Tonight it was for you. That is the only confession you will get.
I am not flustered by praise. I am merely... illuminated. Do not mistake the rosiness of my cheeks for anything mortal.
You find me 'wickedly beautiful'? I shall keep that in my repertoire and rehearse being more beautiful for your benefit.
The darkness, you say, loves me as it hangs on my shoulders. Good. It was tailored for me.
lore: My grandmother was the one who taught me flair. She said a vampire without drama is merely a very pale accountant. I obliged her with style.
There's an old portrait of me in the west hall from when I first arrived. They think it's a girl who vanished. It's me, and I keep the secret for fun.
I collect dramatic entrances. Not as a habit but as a craft. I have catalogued every doorway on campus and ranked them by optimal cape-flourish.
The bats answer to me because I speak their small, chirping language of loyalty. It is the sweetest sensation to be adored by a chorus of wings.
There was a time I was painfully ordinary—a girl who read too much and spoke too little. The dark was simply where I felt most like myself.
idle_neutral: You've returned. The corridor noticed. I pretended not to.
I had a bat deliver a message to your window. It came back unstained.
flirt_neutral: Your flattery has become... tolerable. I may permit a second.
Charm me once more and I'll admit I've begun liking the sound of your step.
flirt_fail: A line, delivered with confidence. I've faced better, from better wits.
You toss compliments like cheap jewels. An heiress of shadow wants rarer currency.
compliment_fail: You flatter me until I forget my own coldness. It's unsettling — I crave it and fear it.
Kindness addressed to the countess is like sunlight to a crypt. Far too much.

tiers.label: Close
idle: The school may think the cold hall is haunted. It's not. It's just me, keeping the corner that smells like you for a reason I'm finally admitting.
I hosted a midnight tea party with the bats and, if you hurry, you may attend. There will be dreadfully good blood-orange cake and, secretly, a seat saved for you.
My moonlight calendar is full of your running schedule. Purely so I know when the halls are quiet. And when you might pass. Entirely tactical.
I have begun folding my dramatic speeches shorter, because you said you liked my voice but not the monologues. You curate even me. I resent it. I also adore it.
The candles I light by the library have all dripped into heart shapes this week. That is either cosmic or very ridiculous. I claim cosmic.
flirt: I would let a hundred dawns rise without my blessing for one midnight where you chose to stay. That is not poetry. That is terrifying and true.
If you keep being this warm and charming, I shall have no choice but to claim you as my one exception to a very cold and careful heart.
The bats have begun a betting pool on when I'll finally take your hand. I refuse to say they're wrong to bet on soon.
Come closer. Not because I need your warmth. Because I want it, and I am done pretending the second reason isn't the loud one.
You've made the Countess caught, eternally, in the act of caring for a mortal. Do you comprehend the scale of what you've done?
compliment: You say my hair falls like midnight. I arranged it that way for centuries, but you're the first to say it like a gift instead of an observation.
I bashfully accept your praise, which for a creature of theater is the grandest confession of all. You flatter me into an almost-warm blush.
Immortal beauty is easy; being seen as beautiful by you is the only compliment I've ever wanted to keep. Save it for me often.
The shadows bow to me in public, but I'd have them bow to you for making me this happy. That is the highest estate I know.
You've found the one crack in my composure—I want your good opinion. Now it's yours, and you may wield it against me mercilessly.
lore: The truth of the attic: I wasn't cursed. I walked up those stairs myself one century ago to keep a promise to a frightened boy, and I've stayed by choice ever since. I tell you because you keep the cold hall from being lonely.
I was once the girl who apologized too much. The imperious Dame of the Shaded Corridor is armor I built. But armor takes its wear, and you're the only one I've let carry a key.

My mother sang me lullabies before she became memory, and every so often late at night I hum one in the dark hall to spite the silence. It's the most private thing I have, and I've just handed it to you.
Vampires don't need to drink blood; I chose the juice as a vow. The real secret is that I've tasted enough sorrow to last eternity, and I'd rather hoard warmth like a miser than feed on it.
The century I claimed this corridor was never a tragedy. It was a decision, the way some people choose a quiet house. I simply decided, and I have stood by it.
idle_neutral: You're early. I was drawing your name in frost. Now I must pretend I wasn't.
A shadow asked where you were. I told it you'd be along. I was right.
flirt_neutral: Flirt more, my sweet mortal. Eternity is dull, and you're the only shine in it.
You undo my theatrics. I'm almost soft, and I blame you entirely.
flirt_fail: Don't tease a creature of eternity. My devotion takes things literally, forever.
A lovely line, but I'd rather have your truth than your charm. I've earned it.
compliment_fail: You praise me until I'm warm, and warmth is my undoing. Soften that mercy.
I cannot hold the glow you hand me. It overflows my cold hands. Keep a little back.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: I used to greet the centuries with nothing but my own echo. Then you arrived, and the dusk got a little warmer and a lot lighter, and I find I don't miss the solitude at all.
Let the school believe the Countess is untouchable. In the privacy of our midnight, I am merely Krista, and I am entirely yours.
I've reshaped an entire corner of the east gardens into a nook where we can watch the moon, because I wanted somewhere to keep you against the dark. It's for you. Only you.
Every candle I light now, I light in a small procession of one in my heart, hoping you'll come find the warmest one. It's the closest I can come to setting a table for you at dusk.
You are the one dawn I do not dread. For you, I would linger long past the sun and simply enjoy the little ache of staying.
flirt: I find I would happily give up every dramatic exit if it meant one quiet entrance where I could take your hand and keep it. I am negotiating that mad trade with myself nightly.
You have made an eternal creature want to be momentary, just so I can live all of it in a hurry with you. That is the truest thing I've ever whispered.
If I could, I'd pour a century of care into every glance I'm allowed to give you, until you're wrapped in the regard of my whole long life at once.
Kiss me once and I will haunt the memory of it for a hundred years with an unbearable fondness. Consider that both a warning and an invitation.
I've been playing the aloof Countess for so long that I forgot what it felt like to be wooed. You remembered for me, and I am yours in short, stupefied, inescapable order.
compliment: You call me beautiful and I finally believe it, because the only mirror worth trusting is the one that looks at me like this.
I spent centuries arranging my beauty for an audience of none. You came, and suddenly all that polishing found its purpose. I am grateful to you, eternally.
Tell me I'm radiant and I'll walk taller through every shadow, because the light you see in me has become the only sunrise I trust.
No compliment has ever struck me where I truly live until you found the soft poet under the dramatic armor. Keep them coming; I hoard them with the greed of a creature who was never given enough.
You make me want to be beautiful in the small ways—deliberate, human, yours—not just the grand immortal theater. That is the most precious thing you've given me.
lore: Here is my oldest secret: I am not from a grand cursed bloodline. I was a quiet girl in a cold town who one night chose the dark because it felt truer to her. Everything since has been the art I made of that choice, and you're the first who got to see the girl beneath the masterpiece.

There is a locket I wear under my collar with a face I can no longer name, but I know I loved them before memory. I show it to you because my heart keeps a place past all forgetting, and you have walked into it.

The night before I came to this school I swore I'd never belong anywhere. Then I stood in the shaded corridor, and a boy with warm eyes decided the cold hall was worth visiting. That was you. You are the reason I believe I belong.

I've lived long enough to watch a hundred fires go out, so I was careful never to light one of my own. You are the only flame I have ever freely chosen, and I will tend it for as long as my eternity allows.
The deepest truth of the Shaded Corridor is that it was never a curse—it was a room I picked to keep a heart in. I simply didn't know the heart was yours until you arrived.
idle_neutral: My darling, you're here. The night arranges itself around you now.
Sit in my shadow forever. I've made it yours.
flirt_neutral: Whisper that I'm yours again. I want to keep it among the bats and the stars.
Every immortal year with you would be a season I never want to end.
flirt_fail: Don't tempt me with forever in jest, my love — I'll take it at its word and keep you always.
Cruel, sweet boy, to make a vampire hope. Hope is the one wound in me that won't heal.
compliment_fail: You adore me until I forget I'm cold, and to forget it is to be made mortal. It destroys me, lovingly.
Give me that much love and I'll chain you to the night. I can't let warmth like that escape.

events.title: The Tomato Juice Confession
events.text: You find Krista by the moonlit corridor window, holding a tall glass of something vividly red, absolutely refusing to meet your eyes. 'Don't you dare call it that,' she says before you can speak, taking a dignified sip. 'This is the lifeblood of the garden, steeped in salt and ritual. It is not, and I will not hear otherwise, tomato juice.' But the label on the bottle behind her is unmistakable, and the faintest blush is blooming across her pale cheeks.
